proof.text: Choose a point $y'\in P\times_ST$ above $x$, possible since $T\to S$ stays surjective after base change, and write $y\in Y$ for its other image. Choose a quasi-affine open $V\subseteq Y$ containing the orbit of $y$. The cover $A\times_ST\to T$ is fpqc. Its pullback represents $F$ by $P\times_ST$, so local finite presentation descends to $Y\to T$. The quasi-compact separated scheme $V$ is consequently of finite presentation over the affine $T$: its morphism is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by qcqs permanence. Write $T=\varprojlim Q_i$ with $Q_i$ finite and finitely presented over $S$ and finite transition maps. Every $Q_i\to S$ is surjective, since the surjection $T\to S$ factors through it. The chart-spreading lemma gives a quasi-affine finite-presentation scheme $V_i$ and an open subfunctor $h_{V_i}\subseteq F_{Q_i}$ pulling back to $h_V$.

source.place: Theorem 4.1, reduction 3, pp.5-19--5-20; adapted to the already Noetherian affine base. Scan https://www.numdam.org/item/SAC_1967-1968__2__A5_0.pdf

proof.text: Put $C_j=\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\times_SQ_j$ for $j\geq i$, and $C=\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\times_ST$. The $x$-section of $F$ gives maps $C_j\to F_{Q_j}$, with open inverse images $E_j$ of $(V_i)_{Q_j}$. Every point of $C$ maps into $V$: its image in $Y$ is in the orbit of $y$. Indeed take a common residue-field extension with the chosen point $y'$ over $x$; the resulting pair of $T$-coordinates is an arrow of the canonical relation on $Y$, from $y$ to that image. Existence of this point is surjectivity of base change of a field spectrum, and the assertion is independent of the common extension. The affine $C_j$ are finite schemes over a field, hence Noetherian; each open $E_j$ is constructible. The limit-contained-in-constructible theorem, applied to $C_j$ and $E_i$, therefore allows us to increase $i$ so that $E_i=C_i$.

source.place: Theorem 4.1, reduction 3, p.5-19: arrange that the finite-stage chart contains the whole fibre over the chosen point; adapted to the already Noetherian affine base. Scan https://www.numdam.org/item/SAC_1967-1968__2__A5_0.pdf

proof.text: Set $Q=Q_i$. On $F_Q$, write $s,t$ for the two relation maps, with domain $F_Q\times_SQ$. These maps are finite on scheme tests, being base changes of $Q\to S$. Define $Z=V_i\setminus s(t^{-1}(F_Q\setminus V_i))$: here $t^{-1}(F_Q\setminus V_i)$ is closed in the scheme $s^{-1}(V_i)=V_i\times_SQ$, and $s$ is finite, so its image is closed in $V_i$. Thus $Z$ is an open subscheme of $V_i$. Its points are exactly those for which every transport lands in $V_i$. Identity, inverse and the triple-overlap cocycle imply that a point and any one of its transports have the same set of further transports: compose with that arrow in one direction and with its inverse in the other. Common residue-field extensions realize the composed arrows. Hence the two inverse images of $Z$ agree on every scheme test, as open subfunctors. This argument uses the canonical transports of the sheaf, without presuming $F_Q$ is a scheme. The image $z$ of $y$ in $V_i$ lies in $Z$. To check this last assertion, pull the fibre $C_i$ back to the residue field of $y'$: all its points already lie in $V_i$ by step 2, and their images give the whole orbit of $z$, using the same common-field-extension argument. Since $Q$ is finite over Noetherian $S$, $V_i$ is Noetherian, and its open $Z$ is quasi-compact and of finite presentation over $Q$. It is quasi-affine, being a quasi-compact open of $V_i$.

source.place: Theorem 4.1, reduction 3: finite closed-map saturation inside the approximated chart, pp.5-19--5-20; adapted to the already Noetherian affine base. Scan https://www.numdam.org/item/SAC_1967-1968__2__A5_0.pdf

proof.text: In $P_Q=P\times_SQ$, let $Z_A$ be the open induced by $h_Z\subseteq F_Q$. The projection $g_A:P_Q\to P$ is finite surjective. Set $P_0=P\setminus g_A(P_Q\setminus Z_A)$. Invariance of $Z$ makes $Z_A$ a union of entire $g_A$-fibres: two lifts of any point of $P$ acquire a common residue field and hence an arrow of the relation, so membership is the same. Therefore $g_A^{-1}P_0=Z_A$, and $x\in P_0$ by step 2. The two pullbacks of $P_0$ to the canonical relation over $A\times_SA$ agree: after the surjective base change by $Q$ both are the open defined by the same section of $F_Q$ and $Z$. Define $F_0(H)$ to consist of sections of $F(H)$ whose pullbacks to $H\times_SA$ land in $P_0$. The equalizer condition shows this is a subfunctor, with $(F_0)_A=h_{P_0}$ and $(F_0)_Q=h_Z$. It is again an fpqc sheaf, as step 6 needs: if $\{H_k\to H\}$ is an fpqc covering and a section of $F(H)$ restricts into $F_0(H_k)$ for all $k$, then the open of $H\times_SA$ pulled back from $P_0$ contains the images of the $H_k\times_SA$, which cover $H\times_SA$ by base change of the jointly surjective covering; so it is everything, and $F_0$ inherits the equalizer condition of $F$. Its pullback to $T$ is represented by the open $Y_0=Y\times_FF_0$: on the fpqc cover $Y\times_SA\to Y$ the prescribed opens agree, so open-subscheme descent applies.

source.place: Theorem 4.1, reduction 3, invariant shrinking and its pullbacks, p.5-20; adapted to the already Noetherian affine base. Scan https://www.numdam.org/item/SAC_1967-1968__2__A5_0.pdf

proof.text: The quasi-affine $Z$ is separated, and its morphism to the affine $Q$ is separated. Thus $Z_A\to A$ is separated. The finite surjection $Z_A\to P_0$ is universally closed, so separatedness of $P_0\to A$ follows from the universally-closed-surjection separation theorem. Also $Z_A$ is quasi-compact: $Z$ and $A$ are quasi-compact over affine $S$, and $Z_A=Z\times_SA$. Its continuous surjective image $P_0$ is quasi-compact, directly by pulling back any open cover. The open $P_0\subseteq P$ is locally of finite presentation over $A$, and separatedness gives quasi-separatedness. Hence $P_0\to A$ is separated and of finite presentation.

source.place: Theorem 4.1, reductions 2--3, separated finite-presentation open model; adapted to the already Noetherian affine base. Scan https://www.numdam.org/item/SAC_1967-1968__2__A5_0.pdf

proof.text: Apply representation spreading to $F_0$, its fpqc cover $A\to S$, and a directed presentation of the affine $A$ as an inverse limit of affine finitely presented $S$-schemes. Such a presentation is obtained by taking the quotients of finite polynomial algebras by finite sets of relations true in $\Gamma(A,\mathcal O_A)$, ordered by enlargement; every element and every relation occurs, so the ring colimit is $\Gamma(A,\mathcal O_A)$. We obtain an affine finitely presented $B\to S$, a map $a:A\to B$, a separated finitely presented $X\to B$ and a representation $(F_0)_B\simeq h_X$, whose pullback identifies $X\times_BA$ with $P_0$. The two representations of $(F_0)_{B\times_SQ}$ give $Z\times_SB\simeq X\times_SQ$: on every test scheme this is the identity on its $F_0$-section and its ordered $B,Q$ coordinates. This formula also identifies the datum on $Z$ after base change by $B$ with the canonical datum on $X\times_SQ$, since both transports keep the same section and change only the $Q$ coordinate. The projection $g:Z_B\to X$ is finite integral surjective, as the base change of $Q\to S$.

source.place: Theorem 4.1, reduction 4 and compatibility (***) in reduction 5, p.5-20; adapted to the already Noetherian affine base. Scan https://www.numdam.org/item/SAC_1967-1968__2__A5_0.pdf

proof.text: The orbit $E$ of $z$ in $Z$ is finite: its relation has finite source map, so the fibre over $z$ is a finite set and its target image is finite. It is saturated by the orbit lemma and is contained in the quasi-affine scheme $Z$. Apply the finite-datum semilocal lemma to obtain an affine $L$ and an invariant quasi-compact flat monomorphism $j:L\to Z$ whose image is $\operatorname{Gen}_Z(E)$. This proves both its generalization stability and equality of its two pullbacks under $D$. The chosen point above $x$ in $P_0\times_SQ$ maps to $z\in E$. After its map to $Z_B\simeq X\times_SQ$, it lies above the image of $x$ in $X$ and has $Z$-coordinate $z\in j(L)$. The base-change image formula therefore puts it in $j_B(L\times_SB)$, proving the required incidence $\operatorname{im}(x)\in g(j_B(L\times_SB))$. All four groups of data have now been constructed, without any quasi-affine enlargement of $j(L)$.
